extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and IP practitioners dealing with Indian patent prosecution and opposition procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules under the Indian Patents Act governing examination (FER), amendments, applicant changes, secrecy directions, pre- and post-grant oppositions, remedies, and register entries for patent applications and granted patents in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for anticipation by prior claiming (S.18(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: On or after the priority date of the applicant’s claim the remedy for the anticipation by prior claiming as explained above will equally apply to this (S.18(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an earlier claim anticipates the later claim, the statutory remedy described for anticipation by prior claiming applies from the relevant priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller power to direct insertion/deletion of reference to another patent (S.19; Rules 32,33)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller has the power to direct the insertion (in the specification) of the reference to another patent which could be infringed in the event of performing the invention of the application, and also for the deletion of such reference from there on request from the applicant, when the said referred patent ceases, or revoked or relevant conflicting claim is deleted from the other patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller may require specification to reference potentially infringed patents; applicant may request deletion when conflicting patent ceases or is revoked; Rules 32/33 govern procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-conclusiveness of Section 13 investigations (S.13(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation made under Section 13 is not deemed to be conclusive on the question of anticipation and central government or its officers incur no liability (S.13(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 13 investigations are informational and do not bind the Controller; no liability attaches to the Central Government/officers for conclusions of such investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Examination Report (FER) communication and opportunity to be heard (S.14; R.24(B), R.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The gist of the objections in the First Examination Report (FER) made by the Examiner will be communicated to the applicant. If any of the objections requires amendment the applicant will be given an opportunity of being heard if the report is adverse to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections requiring amendment are returned with the FER. Applicant can be heard if they request; amendments must comply with Rule 14 and S.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended specification examined like original (S.13(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The amended specification should be examined in the same way as the original specification (S.13(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amendments are subject to the same substantive examination standards as original filings; multiple correspondences may occur after FER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to put application in order after FER (S.21(1); Sec 21(3); Rule 24B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for meeting the objections and putting the application in order is 6 months from the date of issue of FER. This time may be extended only once for a further period not exceeding 3 months by the Controller in circumstances beyond the control of the applicant when a request is made in FORM 4 with specified fee before expiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to meet objections within 6 months (or allowed extension), application will be deemed abandoned. Older cases (FER issued before Patents (Amendment) Act 2005) may have twelve months (Rule 24B(4)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-dating of application (S.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for patent may be post-dated to a date not later than six months from the date of the application on request of the applicant (made at any time before the grant of patent) along with the prescribed fee (Rs.500 for natural person(s) and Rs.2000 for other than natural person(s)). This provision will not apply if the application is deemed abandoned as per S.9(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-dating must be requested before grant and within 6 months; fees differ for natural persons and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller power to deem filing/amendment date on compliance or re-filing (S.17(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application or specification (or drawings) is amended under section 15 to comply with the requirements and the Controller feels that post-dating is required he may direct that such documents be deemed to have been made on the date on which the requirements are complied with or the date on which it is re-filed after complying with the requirements (S.17(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller may retroactively fix filing dates for amended/re-filed documents to the compliance/re-file date when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of applicant — form, proof and consent requirements (S.20; Rule 34-36)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for substituting an applicant has to be made in Form 6 with prescribed fee along with the original assignment/agreement or an official/notarized copy. The Controller may call for other proof of title or written consent of the assignor(s) if required. Direction to substitute an applicant will not be given unless all the applicants have consented to assign the said rights to the claimant (S.20(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments should reference the patent application number or include a statement that they relate to the same invention (S.20(3)). For survivor requests, Form 6 must include legal representative consent, proof of death, and proof of standing (S.20(4); Rule 35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of application and specification — leave, form and fees (S.57; Rule 81(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant or patentee may amend the application, complete specification or any document related thereto after taking leave for amendment in Form13. If the amendment is requested before grant the fee is Rs.500 (natural) and Rs.2000 (others); after grant fees are higher (Rs.1000/Rs.4000). For mere changes of name/address etc. the fee is Rs.200 and Rs.800 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application should state the nature of proposed amendment (usually highlighted in red) and give full particulars of the reason. Priority date of a claim may be amended (S.57(5)). Proof required for change of name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive amendment restriction — no added matter or expanded claim scope (S.59(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment can be allowed only if it is by way of disclaimer, correction or explanation for incorporation of actual fact. Amendment should not be allowed if the specification as amended claims or describes matter not in substance disclosed or shown before the amendment or the amended claims do not fall wholly within the scope of a claim of the specification before the amendment (S.59(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No introduction of new matter or enlargement of claim scope beyond original disclosure; amended pages must be filed in duplicate with duly cancelled originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant substantive amendments published and open to opposition (S.57(3),(4); S.59(2); R83; Rule81(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment is made after grant and the nature is substantive the application should be published in the official journal inviting opposition and permitted amendments will be notified in the Official Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive post-grant amendments are published; interested parties may oppose such amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller refrain from orders during pending infringement/revocation suits (S.57(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is any suit for the infringement or revocation of the patent pending before a court, the Controller shall not pass any order allowing or refusing the application for amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller's power to allow/refuse amendments is stayed while court litigation on the patent is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condonation of irregularities and extension of time (Rule137; Rule138)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document for which no special provision is made may be amended and any irregularity in procedure may be condoned by the Controller on a petition under Rule 137 with prescribed fee (Rs.1000 for natural person, Rs.4000 for others). The Controller has power to extend prescribed time, normally not more than one month and only once in a particular matter (Rule 138(1)); requests must be made within the extendable period and accompanied by prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition/fees required; Controller's extension power is limited in duration and frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of patent once official requirements met (S.21/related)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent may be granted by the Controller at any time, but as soon as possible after the applicant has met with all the official requirements within the period specified in section 21 (6 months from date of FER or within extended period). There is no need to make the request for grant separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting formal and substantive requirements within statutory periods triggers grant; separate request for grant not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy directions — Controller authority for defence-relevant inventions (S.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller may give direction for prohibiting or restricting the publication of information relating to certain inventions if it appears that the invention is of a class notified by Central Government as relevant for defence or the Controller considers it relevant for defence purposes. The Controller will notify the Central Government of such direction (S.35(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy directions can be initiated by Controller or Central Government; they prevent publication/communication to specified persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central Government review and revocation of secrecy direction (S.35(2); S.36; Rule72(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Central Government considers publication would not be prejudicial to defence it will inform the Controller who will revoke the secrecy direction and inform the applicant. Central Government will review relevance at intervals not exceeding 6 months or on reasonable applicant request; results communicated within fifteen days of receipt of notice by Controller (Rule72(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic review mechanism exists; foreign applicant published inventions lead to revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of secrecy direction (non-publication, solatium, fee waiver, time extension) (S.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period when the secrecy direction is in force, the application will not be published. Central Government may make payment of a suitable sum (solatium) if applicant suffers hardship, having regard to novelty and utility. If a patent is granted for an invention under secrecy direction, no renewal fee is payable for the period the direction was in force. When direction revoked, Controller may extend time for acts under the Act up to the duration the direction was in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy leads to non-publication and potentially compensation and waiver of renewal fees for the secrecy period; Controller may retroactively extend deadlines when secrecy revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing abroad without permission (S.39; Rule71)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person resident in India shall not make an application outside India for a patent for an invention without prior permission of the Controller. If an Indian application was made six weeks before filing abroad and no secrecy direction is in force (or revoked), the applicant may proceed abroad. For inventions relevant to defence or atomic energy Controller shall not grant permit without prior consent of Central Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission request made in Form 25 with prescribed fee (Rs.1000 for natural person, Rs.4000 for legal entity); Controller ordinarily disposes within three months; non-defence/atomic inventions often granted within 7 working days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties and finality for violation of secrecy directions (S.40; S.41; S.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contravention of secrecy directions causes the application to be deemed abandoned and any patent granted shall be liable to revocation under Section 64(1)(n). Additional penalties under section 118 (imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both) may apply. All orders of Controller or Central Government under the secrecy chapter are final and not subject to challenge in court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict consequences for breaches; secrecy orders are final administrative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-grant opposition — grounds (S.25(1) clauses a–k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application has been published but not granted, any person may within 6 months from publication represent opposition on specific statutory grounds: wrongful obtaining; prior publication before priority date; prior claim in another Indian complete specification; prior public knowledge/use in India; obviousness/lack of inventive step; subject-matter not an invention or not patentable; insufficient/unclear description; failure to disclose or false information under section 8; convention application timing breach; incorrect or missing source/geographical origin of biological material; anticipation by traditional/indigenous knowledge — but on no other ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds are exhaustive (including substantive requirements like novelty, inventive step, industrial application and statutory exclusions). Controller will hear if requested and dispose per rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects to evaluate in pre-grant opposition — sufficiency of description
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Specification must fully and particularly describe the invention; disclose the best method by which the invention is to be performed; disclose the source and geographical origin of biological material used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficiency includes best method and biological-source disclosure where applicable; these are mandatory pre-grant evaluation points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects to evaluate in pre-grant opposition — subject-matter and exclusions (Sections 2/3/4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject-matter must: constitute an 'invention' under Section 2; have novelty; involve inventive step; be capable of industrial application. Exclusions under Section 3 (and other parts) include: frivolous claims contrary to natural laws; contrary to public order or morality; mere discovery of principle or living thing as occurring in nature; mere new property or new use; mere admixtures; mere arrangement/rearrangement/duplication; methods of agriculture/horticulture; therapeutic/medical treatment processes; plants and animals and essentially biological processes; mathematical/business methods or computer program per se; literary/ artistic works; schemes/rules/methods of performing mental acts; presentation of information; topography of integrated circuits; inventions that effectively are traditional knowledge or aggregation of known properties of traditionally known components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are principal patentability and exclusion criteria to be applied in pre- and post-grant oppositions; the list must be checked against current statutory definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timelines for filing opposition (pre- and post-grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-grant: any person can file opposition by representation within three months from date of publication or before grant, whichever is later. Post-grant: any person interested may give notice of opposition within one year from the date of publication of grant, using prescribed manner and Form-7 with fee (Rs.1500 natural, Rs.6000 legal entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition must include statement and evidence; grounds must be stated in the notice; copy of statement/evidence must be delivered to patentee. Filing forms, fees, and time limits are strictly applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'person interested' for opposition standing (S.2(1)(t))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Person interested' includes a person engaged in or promoting research in the same field as the invention, organizations with manufacturing or trading interest in goods connected with the patented article, persons with financial interest in manufacturing such goods, or who possess patents relating to same subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standing is broad — competitors, researchers, and commercial parties can be 'person interested'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence exchange timelines and restrictions in opposition (Rules 58–60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee must send reply statement covering all grounds with evidence to the appropriate office with a copy to the opponent within 2 months from receipt of copy of written statement and opponent's evidence (Rule 58). The opponent can file reply with evidence within one month and evidence must be strictly confined to matters in the patentee’s evidence (Rule 59). No further evidence shall be delivered except with leave/direction of the Controller (Rule 60).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict, short timelines for exchange of evidence; additional evidence requires Controller leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition board composition, recommendations and hearing procedure (Sec.25(3); Rules 56,62)
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of notice of opposition Controller will constitute an opposition board of three Members who submit recommendations to the Controller after examining opponent’s evidence and patentee’s reply. Controller may fix a hearing after receiving recommendations, giving at least ten days' notice to both parties (Rule 62).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board's recommendations inform Controller decision; parties have statutory hearing rights and may request to be heard (fee applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be heard and fees for hearing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If any party desires to be heard they can file a request to the Controller along with fees (Rs.1500 natural person/Rs.6000 legal entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must pay prescribed fee to secure a hearing; Controller will consider oral submissions along with written record and board recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee withdrawal after opposition and possible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of opposition, if the patentee desires to withdraw the patent, he shall inform the Controller in writing and the Controller, depending upon the merits, may decide whether costs should be awarded to the opponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal may result in costs being awarded against patentee; Controller has discretion based on case merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for wrongful obtaining (S.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Controller refuses the application on ground of wrongful obtaining, he may direct the application to proceed in the name of the opponent with benefit of priority date. If only part of the invention was obtained, Controller may allow amendment excluding that part and opponent may file an application for the excluded part with the same priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller can transfer prosecutorial rights/priority to opponent or require exclusion of wrongfully obtained matter and allow opponent to pursue it as independent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of patents — entries and particulars (S.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon grant of a patent the Controller will enter in the register: name, address and nationality of grantee, title of invention (including categories), date of patent and date of granting, and address for service. Other particulars (assignments, transmissions, licences, amendments, extensions, revocation, cessation, restoration, renewal fee payment, term, surrender, compulsory licences) may also be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register entries provide public record of patent ownership and status; Controller may enter proceedings before Controller or courts in respect of each patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to alter register entries and additional address for service
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may request in writing to the Controller to alter his name, nationality, address or address for service as entered in the register; the Controller may require proof before acting. A request to enter an additional address for service in India may be allowed but no more than two addresses for service shall be entered at any one time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof may be required; Controller has discretion to allow changes and limit addresses for service to two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register as evidence in court — certified copies sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Register of patent can be used as evidence in court; duly certified copies of the entries serve the purpose and original register need not be produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified entries are admissible proof of patent particulars and register status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments etc. not valid unless in writing and registered (S.69)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for registration of assignments, mortgages, licences or other interests affecting patent proprietorship must be made in Form 16 with prescribed fee. Presentation must be accompanied by two copies of the assignment/document certified true copies; Controller may call for further proof of title or written consent as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration in the register is required to make assignments/interest effective against third parties; Form16 and certified copies are mandatory, Controller may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for registration of title or interest after application
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of an application under S.69 the Controller shall register the title of the person concerned or his interest in a patent and make appropriate entry in the register in the prescribed form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration completes the public record; follow-up may be required to ensure entry is made and certified.
